newsitem.title: USA: Medical Technology sees $850,000 Q1 revs.
newsitem.headline: Medical Technology sees $850,000 Q1 revs.

text.p: Medical Technology & Innovations Inc said on Monday it expects to report revenues of about $850,000 for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30.
This compares with revenues of about $155,000 in its fiscal first quarter a year ago.

The big boost to the company's revenues comes from its August acquisition of Steridyne Corp, which will account for about $600,000 of the company's fiscal first quarter sales, Medical Technology chief executive Jeremy Feakins said in an interview.
The Lancaster, Pa.-based company is projecting fiscal 1997 revenues totalling $11.6 million, up from $696,000 in fiscal 1996, with earnings per share rising to an $0.11 profit from a loss of $0.12.
The company makes and sells a hand-held camera known as the PhotoScreener used to detect "lazy eye" syndrome and other vision problems in small children.
Film for the device is made and supplied to Medical Technology by Polaroid Corp.
The Steridyne unit makes pediatric and general health products including electronic thermometers.
